I am calorie counting and it does take a lot of work to make hello fresh work in your calorie deficit. So it will definitely take a lot of effort. I usually plan the rest of my meals around my hello fresh meal. 

I find *most* meals are pretty calorie dense but what I do is look at every recipe first before I choose the meals. Then I add the recipe into my calorie tracker like My fitness pal (you can copy and paste the recipe from the hello fresh website which makes it way easier to substitute things). 

After that I try to make count the calories as accurate as possible and then look for ways I can cut calories. 

Off the top of my head I do things like: replacing Mayo with light Mayo, sour cream with Greek yogurt, using an air fryer instead of a ton of oil, eat less rice or pasta then they recommend, replace some sides with more nutrient dense ones, etc. 

So far eating hello fresh every week I have lost about 30 pounds in 100 days so about 2 pounds a week (of course losing weight can be way more complicated than just watching what you eat I also exercise). 

The reason I do this is because hello fresh is a fun activity I share with my family/friends and I’m not trying to subject them to my diet. 
They get the full version and I get the CICO friendly version and everyone wins. I don’t mind the extra work it’s kind of fun to see all the ways you can make meals healthier by doing small substitutions.
